items.b: Through its subsidiary Iris 2, the radar-satellite operator announced a voluntary offer for all ordinary shares of the Colleferro group that builds the Vega launcher and Ariane motors: €41 in cash, 20% above the 16 November close and 23% above the €33.40 of the reserved capital increase subscribed by Advent in September, for an outlay of up to €2.05bn. The offer is conditional on a 66.67% threshold and on Golden Power, European Commission and CFIUS approvals; Iceye pledges €1bn of investment in Italy over five years and up to 400 new jobs. Leonardo, the largest shareholder with 18.04%, said it was surprised and will assess the deal with the government; the stock closed at €39.39 and Mediobanca considers the price below its €44 target. Why it matters: a bid for a strategic asset is decided by political clearance more than by the premium, and the market prices it below the offer; in the mid-market too, an owner selling a company in sensitive sectors (defence, space, infrastructure) must build Golden Power into the timeline and the conditions of the contract.

items.t: Engineering closes the sale of 100% of the Industries eXcellence Group to Accenture: signed on 17 June, closing after Antitrust and Golden Power clearance, price undisclosed and collected entirely in cash
items.b: The Italian digital services group has completed the sale to Accenture of the subsidiary that develops digital solutions for industry, with operations concentrated in the United States and some European markets; the agreement had been announced on 17 June together with the sale of Alfahealth, which closed on 8 October. Together the two units accounted for about 18% of the group's 2025 revenue (€1,759.7m) and 25% of adjusted EBITDA (€280.3m). The consideration was not disclosed; the proceeds, net of costs and adjustments, were paid in cash and will go first to reducing debt. Why it matters: selling a profitable unit to cut debt and refocus the group is a choice an SME with several business lines can make too; it requires a cleanly separated perimeter and, as here, five months between signing and closing for the approvals.

items.t: Grote Company (BBH Capital Partners) closes the purchase of 100% of Turatti (Cavarzere): Green Arrow Capital and Entangled Capital exit, €26.7m revenue, price undisclosed but estimated at about €15.7m
items.b: The Columbus, Ohio group, which makes machinery and automation for the food industry and is backed by the BBH Capital Partners fund, has completed through Grote Company Italia the acquisition of the entire share capital of Turatti srl, a maker of fruit and vegetable processing lines with two plants in Veneto and an operating base in Salinas, California. The sellers are Green Arrow Capital's Taste of Italy fund, Entangled Capital and some managers; the agreement was signed in early September and closing, subject to Italian government clearance, was formalised with the share transfer deed. Turatti ended 2025 with €26.7m in revenue and €3.6m EBITDA, and CEO Enrico Gribaudo stays at the helm. The price was not disclosed: BeBeez puts it at about €15.7m, just over 4x EBITDA if the estimate is right. Why it matters: more than two months passed between signing and closing for the government clearance, which now covers industrial plants for the food sector as well; an owner selling to a foreign buyer should plan for that timeline and, as here, commit the management team to staying on to make continuity credible.

items.t: Xenon FIDEC creates Thexion with majority stakes in five cybersecurity companies (Exi, Dinets, Stone Security, RJ45Lab, Evolumia): €80m aggregate revenue, founders reinvest, €40m unitranche from Generali
items.b: The private equity fund focused on the energy and digital transition has acquired majority stakes in five Italian companies and combined them into Thexion, a hub for protecting critical infrastructure in energy and telecoms with more than 600 professionals: Exi of Rome (€23.2m 2025 revenue), Dinets of Ancona (€21.3m), Stone Security of Rome (€5.9m), RJ45Lab of Pescara (penetration testing and red teaming) and Evolumia of Triggiano, Bari (€2.8m, up 89%). The founders reinvested and remain shareholders; each company keeps its own brand with the tag 'a Thexion company'. Generali AM Direct Private Debt financed the consolidation with a €40m unitranche; Belluzzo International Partners, Deloitte and Ethica Debt Advisory advised Xenon, Dentons the lender. Prices of the individual acquisitions were not disclosed; the deal comes days after the same fund's €85m purchase of Deas. Why it matters: in a fragmented sector like cybersecurity, funds buy five companies of €3-25m in one go to build a platform; for the founder of an IT services SME, a sale can become entry into a larger group, with a reinvested minority stake and the prospect of a second payout when the fund exits.

items.t: The Italian Sea Group awarded to SRI Global (Gallazzi and Vacchi) for €220m in the composition-with-creditors tender: the Marina di Carrara, La Spezia, Viareggio and Terni yards and the Admiral, Tecnomar, Perini Navi and Picchiotti brands
items.b: The holding company of Giulio Gallazzi and Bernardo Vacchi has won the business complex of the Marina di Carrara luxury yacht group, which is in a going-concern composition with creditors after a 2025 loss of €170.9m and a 27% drop in revenue: the tender before the notary appointed by the Florence court closed on 16 November with no counter-bids, with Azimut-Benetti stopping at €210m and the late offers from Palumbo (€221m) and a Hong Kong vehicle (€250m) excluded. SRI's plan adds €40m of investment, a business lease from 1 December with the transfer of about 500 direct employees, and then the definitive sale; TISG's board meets on 23 November and the court hearing on admission to the procedure is set for 23 December. Unsecured creditors would receive about 10%, shareholders nothing. Why it matters: in an insolvency procedure the winner is whoever follows the rules and deadlines, not whoever offers the most, as the exclusion of two higher bids shows; a buyer looking at a distressed company must show up before the deadline with proof of funds, a business plan and union agreements, because afterwards there is no room to catch up.

items.t: Nextchem (Maire) buys Chart Industries' natural gas liquefaction technologies for $220m: more than 90 patents, high-single-digit multiple on 2027 EBITDA, closing expected between year-end and January
items.b: Maire's subsidiary, through Nextchem USA, has signed a binding agreement to acquire from Chart Industries (Baker Hughes group) the IPSMR technology for mid-scale LNG plants, the small-scale solutions, more than 90 patents, the trademarks and a team of 12 specialists, with an installed base of 14 million tonnes a year. The $220m price will be paid at closing with dedicated credit lines underwritten by BPER Banca; the licensing business is expected to generate at least $25m of EBITDA in 2027, a multiple that Citi estimates at around 9x. Closing is expected between the end of 2026 and early January 2027, after regulatory approvals. Why it matters: this is a purchase of a technology and the people who know how to sell it, not a factory; in the mid-market too, an owner carving out a business made of patents and know-how gets better valuations by separating the perimeter cleanly and tying the team that makes it work to the contract.

items.t: Sweden's Indutrade buys 100% of Acoma (Crema): €12m revenue and 32 employees, the group's 14th acquisition of 2026
items.b: The Stockholm-listed industrial group, which controls more than 225 companies, has acquired the entire share capital of Acoma srl, a Crema-based company founded in 2009 that makes printing blankets and coating plates for industrial print, used mainly in food, pharmaceutical and manufacturing packaging. The company generates about €12m in annual sales with 32 staff and joins the Industrial & Engineering business area; closing took place on 12 November, the same day the agreement was signed. The price was not disclosed and the sellers were not named; Indutrade, advised by De Berti Jacchia and KPMG, had already bought CAT Ricambi in February and this is its fifth acquisition in Italy. Why it matters: a serial acquirer like Indutrade looks for niche companies with a distinctive production process (here a solvent-free technology) and a management team that stays on; an owner of a €10-15m SME with a recognisable technical edge has a foreign industrial buyer willing to take 100% and leave operational autonomy.

items.t: Viaemilia Investments (Cherry Bay Capital and Dallara) takes 30% of Bercella for €10m: €11m revenue, 20% EBITDA margin, the family keeps 70%
items.b: The new private-capital vehicle dedicated to Motor Valley companies, promoted by Cherry Bay Capital Partners and the Dallara group, has closed its first investment in Bercella spa of Varano de' Melegari (Parma), a specialist in carbon-fibre and composite structures for motorsport and aerospace with 2025 revenue of €11m and a structural EBITDA margin of around 20%. The deal, announced on 12 November, is worth €10m for 30% of the capital: 80% of the amount goes into a capital increase to fund growth and 20% to the selling shareholders; the Bercella family keeps about 70% and operational leadership. The plan targets 50% growth already in 2026 driven by aerospace, expansion in the United States and possible acquisitions; Viaemilia has raised €50m towards a €100m target and is looking for local companies with up to €50m in revenue. Why it matters: a minority entry made almost entirely through a capital increase puts money into the company rather than the owners' pockets, and is the right tool for a founder who wants to grow without giving up control; having an industrial partner from the supply chain like Dallara on the shareholder register is often worth more than a discount on valuation.

items.t: Canada's Protech Group has acquired 100% of Ripol (Santo Stefano Ticino) from the Di Segni family: value undisclosed, about €29m according to BeBeez
items.b: The Protech Group, a Montreal-based maker of industrial coatings with more than 25 plants worldwide, has acquired through its subsidiary Oxyplast Belgium the entire capital of Ripol srl, which the Di Segni family held through Delta Sigma Investments. The company, founded 25 years ago, makes powder coatings for industrial and architectural applications at its plant just outside Milan and brings with it commercial affiliates in Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain and Switzerland. The deal took effect on 30 October; the parties did not disclose the value, which according to reports published by BeBeez on 13 November would be about €29m, without specifying whether equity or enterprise value. Why it matters: a family-owned SME with a recognised brand and an already-built European sales network is the ideal target for a foreign group that wants to enter a market in one move; for the seller, having opened foreign subsidiaries before the sale translates directly into a higher price.

items.t: IPCOM (Astorg) has bought 100% of Eurofoam (Lainate) from the Sandrini family: price undisclosed, €22.7m according to BeBeez; the brothers stay in charge
items.b: IPCOM Group, a pan-European distributor of technical insulation and energy-efficiency solutions controlled by the private equity fund Astorg, has acquired through IPCOM Italia the entire capital of Eurofoam srl, a Lainate (Milan) company founded in 1965 that manufactures and converts compact rubber, cellular rubber and technical foams for industry. Entry into the group was announced on 21 October; the company will be integrated into the Flexicel business unit and Massimiliano and Gianpaolo Sandrini stay on as CEO and CFO respectively, after the death earlier this year of founder Giancarlo, who had approved the deal. The price was not disclosed: according to BeBeez reports of 13 November it would be €22.7m. Why it matters: when the founder passes away, selling to a private-equity-backed platform that asks the next generation to stay on is a way to cash out without breaking continuity; add-on buyers pay for the combination of a technical product, industrial customers and a management team willing to remain at least through the integration period.

items.t: Luisaviaroma goes to the Andorlini-Corinaldesi consortium for €18.8m: the Florence e-tailer's business sold in a simplified composition procedure, 157 employees retained
items.b: Lvr srl, a newco controlled by the holding company Ato and led by CEO Tommaso Andorlini with Paolo Corinaldesi (formerly Woolrich and Filson) as executive chairman, wins the Luisaviaroma business for €18.8m: the online channel, the stores in Florence, Prato and Forte dei Marmi, the technology platform and the brands, excluding the already-closed New York store. The consortium also includes the Marzotto family, Gian Luca Sghedoni (Litokol), Ettore Riello and Luca Poggi; the competitive process run by the Florence court closed on 8 November with no rival bids, after Mena Marano's Arav group did not formalise its interest. The retailer, exited by private equity fund Style Capital at the end of 2025, was in a simplified liquidation composition procedure; the new owners have run the business under a lease since July, the transfer is expected by the end of November and 157 employees remain out of more than 200. Why it matters: in a distressed situation, the buyer who steps in early through a business lease reaches the auction knowing the numbers, with staff already in place, and often ends up as the only bidder; a seller in a court procedure should expect the price to reflect only the transferable assets, not historical revenue.

items.t: Metriks AI signs the definitive agreement for 100% of Workgroup: €18.9m to Mare Group for 95% in cash, shares and convertible bonds, €20m valuation or 7.5× 2026 EBITDA
items.b: The two Euronext Growth Milan-listed companies have turned the 29 July agreement into a binding contract: Metriks AI buys 95% of Workgroup, the software house and engineering hub of the Mare group, for €18.9m, of which €7m in cash, €1m in new Metriks shares at €4.50 and €10.9m in convertible bonds maturing June 2028; the remaining 5% comes from WGS in exchange for shares worth €1.1m. The €20m valuation for 100% is about 7.5× expected 2026 EBITDA of €2.9m, with net financial position of €2m; if the 2026 targets are missed or not sustained in 2027 a price adjustment hits the convertible only, and if they are exceeded an earn-out of up to €3m in shares kicks in. Closing is expected by the end of 2026, after the Metriks shareholder meeting approves the issues; Antonio Torino stays on as Workgroup CEO and will join the buyer's board, while Mare Group, booking an estimated €5.7m capital gain, redeploys resources into defence and aerospace. Why it matters: when the buyer pays mostly in its own paper, the seller collects little more than a third upfront and ties the rest to the acquirer's share price and the target's results; before accepting shares and convertibles it pays to negotiate, as here, that price adjustments only touch the deferred component and that any upside is rewarded through an earn-out.

items.t: WeRoad buys Swiss start-up TravelTribe and launches an acquisition drive: target of €70m in M&A-driven revenue within three years, price undisclosed
items.b: The Milan-based group-travel company, which in May closed a $58m Series C round led by Airbnb, has acquired the Zurich start-up founded in 2024 by Francesco Lorenzo, a former WeRoad coordinator, and Francesco Staccone: more than 300 trips organised for 1,600 travellers, with ski weekends in Zermatt, Laax and St. Moritz accounting for almost 70% of bookings. Brand, platform and community fold into WeRoad, which strengthens its presence in the DACH region and brings WeMeet, its local-events platform, to Switzerland, with Staccone joining as WeMeet co-founder; financial terms were not disclosed. The deal is framed as the first step of a programme targeting €70m of additional revenue from acquisitions within three years, with group-travel platforms and events companies serving 2,000 to 40,000 customers a year in its sights. Why it matters: a scale-up that has just raised capital turns into a serial buyer of small businesses with loyal communities; for the founder of an SME in the sector this is the moment to have clean numbers ready and, if they want to stay on, to negotiate a role in the project and not just the price.

items.t: GSquare launches tender offer for the remaining 17.33% of Valtecne (Valtellina): €11.87 per share plus earn-out, EV €79.9m or 9.9× 2025 EBITDA
items.b: ValBlue BidCo, a vehicle of the GSquare Healthcare Private Equity fund, opened on 9 November the mandatory tender offer for the 17.33% still on the market of the Valtellina-based precision-mechanics supplier to the medtech industry, listed on Euronext Growth Milan, after closing in September the purchase of 81.84% from the Mainetti family for about €59.3m. The base price is €11.87 per share, with an earn-out of up to €0.82 tied to a future acquisition or to the fund's returns; the offer is worth at most €13.4m and values 100% of the company at €72.5m equity and €79.9m enterprise value, against 2025 revenue of €35.7m and EBITDA of €8.1m. CEO Paolo Mainetti reinvested €22.2m and holds about 45% of the holding company, director Luigi Ferrari €1.8m; acceptances run until 27 November, with delisting as the goal. Why it matters: at 9.9× EBITDA, an owner who sells control to a specialist fund and reinvests almost half of the proceeds gets paid today and keeps a seat at the table; the earn-out offered to minority shareholders shows how part of the price can be tied to future results without stalling the deal.

items.t: Balmaris (Balcaen family) takes a majority of Porto Turistico di Jesolo from Marvit (Marzotto), which keeps a minority: over 600 berths
items.b: Balmaris, a platform set up in 2026 to acquire and run marinas across Europe and backed by Baltisse, the holding of Belgium's Balcaen family, already owner of Moniga Porto Nautica on Lake Garda and a shareholder of Dolciaria Acquaviva, has acquired a majority of the marina at the mouth of the Sile river, seven nautical miles from Venice, with more than 600 berths. The seller is Marvit, Stefano Marzotto's holding, which took control in 2025, invested about €10m in the site and keeps a minority stake to support the next phase. The exact stake, price and revenue were not disclosed; the plan covers the boatyard, hospitality and boat dealerships. Why it matters: after Marina Genova went to D-Marin the day before, this is the second Italian marina sold in a week to a foreign platform: owners of tourism-infrastructure assets now find competing buyers, and staying in as a minority partner with an agreed investment plan is a way to share in the upside.

items.t: Aksìa moves Valsa Group into its first €200m continuation fund and takes joint control with PX3: revenue up from €20m to almost €200m since 2020
items.b: Aksìa sgr and PX3 Partners have completed a joint investment in the premium savoury bakery group built since 2020, when the Aksìa Capital V fund bought Valpizza, through a string of acquisitions that lifted revenue from about €20m to almost €200m. The deal runs through Aksìa CF I, a single-asset continuation fund with about €200m of commitments and Belnord Capital as lead investor, alongside the new Aksìa Capital VI fund and PX3 Fund I; management reinvests and a lender group led by Pemberton provides the debt. Valuation and the split of stakes were not disclosed. Why it matters: a continuation fund lets a fund at the end of its life avoid selling at a discount and stay invested in a company with room to grow; for an owner who sold to a fund, it means the next partner may be the same manager with fresh capital rather than an outside buyer.

items.t: Casa Optima (Terlos and GIC) buys 100% of Dutch distributor Laan Heiloo from Orkla: the MEC3 and Pernigotti distributor has revenue of almost €6m
items.b: The Rimini-based group of ingredients for gelato, pastry and mixology, controlled by an investor consortium led by Terlos with Singapore's sovereign fund GIC after Charterhouse's exit completed in February, signed and closed at the same time the purchase of the long-established Dutch distributor trading as Nic Gelato Nederland, with revenue of about €6m. The seller is Nic Group, a business unit of Orkla Food Ingredients that had bought it in 2017; Laan Heiloo already distributed the group's MEC3 and Pernigotti brands in the Netherlands. The price was not disclosed; it is the first acquisition under the new ownership. Why it matters: buying your own foreign distributor is the most direct way to bring margin and the end-customer relationship in-house; for an SME-sized distributor, the main supplier is often the most natural buyer and worth sounding out before running an auction.

items.t: SYS-DAT buys 60% of Soluzione 1 (Ghisalba): €3.5m expected revenue, put and call options on the remaining 40%
items.b: The ICT company listed on Euronext STAR Milan has acquired 60% of the Bergamo-based firm that digitises business processes for mid-sized and large companies, together with its 80%-owned Milan subsidiary Caplab. For 2026 the two companies expect combined revenue of about €3.5m, EBITDA of €0.3m and a positive net cash position of about €1m; the price was not disclosed. The agreements give the seller a put and SYS-DAT a call on the remaining 40%, exercisable after approval of the 2029 accounts and by 30 April 2030. It is the group's third acquisition this year. Why it matters: with an initial 60% and an exit fixed by options, the seller cashes in part now and ties the rest to the next three years' results, while the buyer limits the risk of overpaying for a small company.

items.t: Hera (AcegasApsAmga) takes 100% of Gigas Rete from Brimsco: 1,200 km of gas network in 23 Verona municipalities, €3.5m EBITDA
items.b: AcegasApsAmga, a subsidiary of the Hera group, has signed a binding agreement for the entire capital of the Lodi-based company, which runs about 1,200 km of network and 57,400 delivery points in the Verona area, with 2025 EBITDA of about €3.5m. The price is not public: the parties indicate an enterprise value in line with the RAB, the regulatory asset base. Closing is expected in the coming months after customary conditions; for Brimsco the sale supports a refocus on energy retail and renewables. Why it matters: in a regulated business the price anchors to an objective benchmark such as the RAB, and a seller disposing of a non-core unit to an operator already present nearby finds a buyer willing to pay for the synergies.

items.t: Club deal led by Findi Investimenti and ANMO takes a majority of Gruppo Poppi (hot forging); the family keeps 45%
items.b: A group of entrepreneurs coordinated by Findi Investimenti and ANMO, Andrea Motori's firm, has acquired a majority of the Emilia-based steel hot-forging and precision-mechanics group, which includes Poppi Ugo Euroforge (Terre del Reno), Elettrostamperie Italia and Italgear (Casalecchio di Reno). Founders Ugo and Paolo Poppi keep 45%; according to reports cited by BeBeez the stake sold is 55%. Price and revenue were not disclosed. A pool of six banks led by Cassa Centrale Banca financed the deal. Why it matters: for a mid-sized family business, a club deal of entrepreneurs is a buyer that accepts leaving a sizeable stake with the founders and brings patient capital without a fund's fixed exit deadline.

items.t: D-Marin (Infravia) buys Marina Genova: €10.4m revenue and over 450 berths, its fifth marina in Liguria
items.b: The Athens-based premium marina group, controlled by Infravia Capital Partners since July, has acquired Marina Genova spa in Sestri Ponente, linked to entrepreneur Dino Rasero through Marina Genova Aeroporto and the holding Heracles. The operating company closed 2025 with €10.4m revenue, about €0.9m EBITDA and €1.4m net debt, while the parent carried €55m of financial debt against €5.7m of equity. Stake and price were not disclosed; closing is subject to regulatory approval. The deal brings D-Marin's network to 30 marinas in nine countries. Why it matters: an asset with solid revenue but an over-indebted holding finds its exit in a strategic buyer that pays for the location, not the balance sheet, and for a seller the debt structure weighs on price as much as the income statement.

items.t: Equinox IV buys 60% of Gruppo Master (Conversano): €65m expected revenue, family keeps 40%
items.b: The Equinox IV fund takes control of the Apulian maker of accessories and components for aluminium windows and doors, founded in 1986, with over 370 employees, 60% of sales abroad and 2026 guidance of about €65m revenue and €10m EBITDA. The Loperfido-Lacatena family keeps 40% and stays in charge of operations; the price was not disclosed. The stated goal is an acquisition plan to build a European group in the sector. Why it matters: a family that sells the majority but keeps 40% and the wheel gets paid today and shares in the second round of value creation, the buy-and-build.

items.t: CPI and Zero Capital club deal takes 100% of Lasertech (Liscate); the Binelli family reinvests
items.b: Haslan Due, a vehicle promoted by Cattaneo Partecipazioni e Investimenti and Zero Capital with entrepreneurs and private investors, has completed the purchase of the whole share capital of the Milan-area specialist in photochemical etching, laser micro-cutting and precision metal components for automotive, medical and electronics clients. The founders reinvest a significant part of the proceeds in the vehicle and Maurizio Binelli stays on as chairman and CEO; Banco BPM financed the deal, whose value and the target's revenue were not disclosed. It is the group's second investment after Storci Perforazioni in 2025. Why it matters: a club deal is an alternative to a fund for an owner who sells everything yet wants to stay a shareholder and keep running the business, with a longer holding period.

items.t: Ivan Glasenberg's holding (Pinarello) enters Campagnolo with 28%: €65.9m revenue, negative EBITDA
items.b: SPAC sa, the Swiss vehicle of the former Glencore CEO and shareholder of Pinarello and Technogym, has completed the investment in the Vicenza maker of groupsets and wheels for road bikes announced on 2 September: according to BeBeez the stake is 28%, with the Campagnolo family (Fidifa) keeping the majority. The deal comes with a reshaped financial structure to back the turnaround plan; the last fiscal year closed with €65.9m revenue and EBITDA of -€12.9m, 259 employees and 90 redundancies still to be managed. The price is not public. Why it matters: in a loss-making company a minority partner bringing capital and a relationship with the banks is worth more than a buyer offering only a price, but comes on terms dictated by the plan.

items.t: Crédit Agricole proposes to Banco BPM a merger with Crédit Agricole Italia: 20% premium and €1bn dividend
items.b: The French group, already at 29.6% of Banco BPM, has proposed to the board led by Giuseppe Castagna to combine the bank with Crédit Agricole Italia and its Italian insurance businesses, creating the country's third banking group with about 6.5 million clients; the French would rise to 45% without an absolute majority and Castagna would stay CEO. BPM shareholders would get an exchange ratio with a 20% premium and a €1bn special dividend; synergies are estimated at €800m a year. The BPM board will discuss it on 12 November; a whitewash shareholder vote, ECB and golden power clearances are needed, with completion pencilled in for the second half of 2027. Why it matters: bank consolidation shrinks the number of lenders SMEs can talk to and changes the counterparts of BPM's corporate clients.

items.t: Mare Group buys 51% of Proser: EV €2.8m, about 4× EBITDA
items.b: The Euronext Growth Milan-listed engineering company takes control of the Rome aerospace electronics firm (€5m revenue, €0.7m expected EBITDA) for €1.6m; closing by December after golden power clearance. Four days earlier it announced Ass.El. Why it matters: this is the real mid-market, deals of a few million at low multiples, where a listed SME acts as a supply-chain consolidator.

items.t: BPCE Assurances in exclusive talks for 100% of GamaLife (Apax), a €600m deal
items.b: The French banking group's insurance arm negotiates for the life platform active in Portugal and Italy; Generali and BFF Bank were also in the race. Why it matters: Italian insurance remains among the sectors most contested by foreign groups.

items.t: Safety21 (Bregal Unternehmerkapital) buys 60% of Smartprise: twelfth add-on since 2021
items.b: The enforcement and collection company, controlled by the German fund since 2021, targets €135m revenue in 2026; the sellers keep 40%, brand and structure. Why it matters: buy-and-build at full stretch, twelve acquisitions in five years, with sellers staying as minority partners.

items.t: Hong Kong's Austen Capital takes 100% of Smart Evolution Trading (vaping)
items.b: The Asian investor, already active in tobacco alternatives in Switzerland and the Middle East, also acquires subsidiary MD Tech. Why it matters: non-EU strategic buyers also look at regulated niches, where local distribution is worth more than the product.

items.t: Siemens completes acquisition of Mermec's key divisions
items.b: Announced in May, the deal brings the Apulian group's rail signalling, electrification, diagnostics and data businesses, including the former Ferrosud plant in Matera, into the German group. Why it matters: a large industrial carve-out where a family group sells its technology arm to a global leader.

items.t: Francisco Partners and KKR enter TeamSystem at a valuation of up to €10bn
items.b: Hellman & Friedman monetises a stake in the SME software group, already through three funds. Why it matters: TeamSystem is the textbook case of Italian vertical software growing by acquisition and passing fund to fund while multiplying value.

items.t: Ancora acquires 100% of Studio Eldas: €878k revenue, owners stay on
items.b: The startup founded in early 2026 by ex-Satispay, Morgan Stanley and L Catterton people buys an accounting firm and reaches €1m recurring revenue; it aims to consolidate more professional practices. Why it matters: roll-ups reach professional firms, so far off the M&A radar. Anyone with a practice and a loyal client base has a new kind of buyer.

items.t: EY: 1,105 deals announced in Italy in nine months, +15%; 56% of fund deals go through portfolio companies
items.b: Private equity and infrastructure funds announced about 525 deals on Italian targets against 422 a year earlier; supply-chain consolidation accounts for 79% of deals. Why it matters: it confirms the BeBeez figures. Today the most likely buyer for an SME is a fund-backed company looking for add-ons.

items.t: Intesa Sanpaolo gets ECB clearance for its offer on MPS
items.b: Prior authorisation also covers the indirect stakes in Mediobanca, Compass and Banca Progetto; Bank of Italy cleared the subsidiaries the same day. With all approvals in hand, the offer enters its final phase. Why it matters: this single banking deal can push the 2026 Italian market past €70bn.

items.t: Sanac: ministry authorises sale of three plants to Erre Trading
items.b: The refractories maker in extraordinary administration is sold in parts; the Assemini site is excluded for now. The deal confirms 180 jobs and 15 hires in 2027. Why it matters: a sale out of insolvency is won on jobs and scope more than on price.

items.t: UAE's EDGE closes purchase of 80% of CMD; the Negri family keeps 20%
items.b: CMD (Potenza and Caserta) makes propulsion systems for automotive, aerospace and marine; about €40m revenue and €5m EBITDA in 2025. Preliminary agreement in May, closing at end of October. Why it matters: in January the family bought back 67% from China's Loncin; nine months later it sells control to a strategic investor and keeps a minority. See the full case.

items.t: Alcedo IV sells majority of cybersecurity firm Nethive to Bregal Milestone
items.b: Alcedo bought 53% of the Padua company in 2021; the founders reinvest and stay co-CEOs. Nethive simultaneously acquires Rome-based JoyComm. Alcedo is raising a €300m Fund VI. Why it matters: a textbook secondary buyout, with first-fund exit, founder rollover and an add-on at closing.

items.t: Private equity: 476 deals in nine months, 65% are add-ons
items.b: BeBeez counts 476 deals announced or closed January to September (159 in Q3), 64% of the whole of 2025. Add-ons are 274, a rising share; 61 target foreign companies. Why it matters: funds increasingly buy small companies to bolt onto their platforms. For an SME, today's most likely buyer is a company already backed by a fund.

items.t: KPMG: a more selective Italian M&A market, 910 deals and €46bn in nine months
items.b: Deals down 17.5% and value down 29% on 2025, but six deals above €1bn in Q3 alone and a pipeline of over €90bn announced. Domestic: 497 deals for €14bn. Why it matters: fewer but larger deals; in the mid-market, selection rewards those who come to market prepared.

items.t: BCG: record number of deals with an Italian party in the first seven months, over 900
items.b: Highest in a decade, +20% on the 2016-2025 average, but value at $39.9bn (-26%). Industrials have the most deals (193) and the lowest value ($1.1bn). Sponsor-backed deal value is up 37%. Why it matters: the Italian market is made of many small deals, exactly the ground for an SME marketplace.
